# Critical polarization and gapless modes — 2026-09-30

**32pi remains OPEN.** This continuation finds a concrete route to the required nonlinear response: an isotropic polarization selected by a static equation, with a positive cubic potential generated by two-dimensional fermion modes. It also calculates the nonlocal correction that a homogeneous treatment would miss. No vacuum-energy normalization or stream-generated population of these modes has been derived.

Base checkpoint: `8fbd56a2c`. The [contract](CRITICAL_RESPONSE_CONTRACT.md) precedes each continuation. This builds on the fixed-orientation obstruction and previous inverse fluctuation construction without calling an inverse-designed potential a prediction.

## 1. Select the polarization by an equation

Consider the static normalized functional

    W(g,p) = |g|²/2 - g dot p + V(|p|),
    L_static = -W/(4pi G) - rho_b Phi,   g = grad Phi.

The internal vector p has acceleration units and is an auxiliary polarization here. For a monotonically increasing convex radial V, minimization aligns p with g and gives V'(p)=g. Eliminating p then gives the induction vector b = g-p, and div b = 4pi G rho_b. Reversing g reverses the selected p and b. This removes the earlier parity obstruction for a *fixed* internal orientation. It is a static equation of state, not a dynamical formation, relaxation or covariant stability proof.

An exact P2 representation is

    V(p) = p²/4 - hp/2 - (h²/2) log(1-p/h),   0 <= p < h.
    g = p(2h-p)/[2(h-p)].

It selects p=g+h-sqrt(g²+h²), hence b=sqrt(g²+h²)-h and a0=2h. The internal potential is convex, with V''=1/2+h²/[2(h-p)²], and polarization saturates at h. Its small-p expansion is p²/2+p³/(6h)+O(p⁴). Eliminating it reproduces the previous static P2 action. This exact potential was reconstructed from P2; no novelty or microscopic selection is claimed.

## 2. Identify the critical term, including the tuning

For V(p)=p²/2+alpha p³, alpha>0, the stationarity equation is

    g = p + 3alpha p²,
    b = g-p = 3alpha p².

As g tends to zero, b=3alpha g²+O(g³), so a0=1/(3alpha). The spherical field equation b=GM/r² gives g approximately sqrt(GM a0)/r: the required square-root mass scaling follows. This cubic-only model is not the full P2 interpolation; it approaches Newtonian induction at large g but with different corrections. Its static radial derivative db/dg=1-1/sqrt(1+12alpha g) is positive for g>0. The tangential derivative b/g is positive as well; ellipticity degenerates in the zero-field limit as in this deep-MOND construction.

An analytic O(3)-invariant potential near p=0 is a series in p². At the same quadratic cancellation, a leading p⁴ term gives b proportional to g³, not g². The p³ here means |p|³, which is nonanalytic as a function of the three vector components. Gapless modes can supply such a term.

The quadratic cancellation remains an assumption. With V=(1+delta)p²/2+alpha p³ and delta>0, b/g tends to delta/(1+delta), restoring a linear low-field response. Its crossover is parametrically near g of order delta a0 for small delta. Thus a mechanism must set or protect delta=0; finding a cubic term alone is insufficient.

## 3. Generate the cubic term and track its dimension

Take nu occupied negative-energy bands in **two spatial dimensions**, with dispersion E_k=sqrt(k²+m²). Subtract the massless vacuum and the analytic quadratic divergence using momentum cutoff K:

    E_ren = -nu[(K²+m²)^(3/2)-K³-|m|³]/(6pi)
            +nu K m²/(4pi).

Its K to infinity limit is +nu |m|³/(6pi). Nine direct radial quadratures cross-check the regulated expression. This is energy per area, not bulk cosmological density. The cubic potential agrees with the independent 2+1-dimensional fermion effective-potential derivation in [Davis, Kraus and Shah, JHEP 11 (2008) 020, Eqs. (2.15)-(2.16)](https://inspirehep.net/files/0168a297cdf680eeef86c0c8f11a6848). The regulator-dependent analytic term is precisely why critical tuning cannot be omitted.

The sign matters: a real thermal boson zero mode in three spatial dimensions instead contributes -T|m|³/(12pi). This follows by differentiating its determinant, subtracting the analytic cutoff term and integrating back. It matches [Quiros, hep-ph/9901312, Eq. (174)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/9901312). That term alone has the wrong sign for the positive alpha above. No statement about all interacting thermal phases follows.

An explicit four-band spectral realization is

    Gamma1 = sigma_x tensor I,     Gamma2 = sigma_y tensor I,
    (Gamma3,Gamma4,Gamma5) = sigma_z tensor (sigma_x,sigma_y,sigma_z),
    H = kx Gamma1 + ky Gamma2 + y sum_i p_i Gamma_(i+2).

The five Hermitian matrices anticommute. H²=(k²+y²|p|²)I, with two negative and two positive bands. Internal rotations generated by products of the last three matrices rotate the mass triplet and preserve both momentum matrices. This realizes the isotropic mass spectrum m=y|p| instead of merely postulating it. It does not explain why galactic streams create such two-dimensional modes or how physical spatial rotations identify with these internal rotations.

If sheets have area per volume 1/ell, then multiplying their energy by 4pi G gives the **hypothetical** normalized coefficient

    alpha = 2G nu y³/(3ell),   a0 = ell/(2G nu y³).

Here nu includes the occupied-band degeneracy and flavor count. Sheet density, y and the renormalized quadratic term remain inputs. A scalar vacuum counterterm survives: changing the absolute vacuum energy changes Lambda while preserving this homogeneous response. In this dictionary the target G rho_vac=4a0² requires the extra condition rho_vac=ell²/(G³ nu² y⁶), which has not been derived.

## 4. Do not discard the spatial response

The same gapless modes produce a nonanalytic massless two-point kernel. The convergent Euclidean bubble is

    I(q,m) = integral d³k/(2pi)³ 1/[(k²+m²)((k+q)²+m²)]
           = atan(q/(2m))/(4pi q).

Independent Feynman-parameter and radial quadratures verify the integral and its massless limit I(q,0)=1/(8q). For one four-band flavor (nu=2), with y=1, subtract the q=0 potential curvature. The static longitudinal and transverse corrections about a **uniform** polarization are

    DeltaPi_L = 2[(q²+4m²) I(q,m) - 4m² I(0,m)],
    DeltaPi_T = 2q² I(q,m).

The traces have numerators proportional respectively to -k dot (k+q)+m² and -k dot (k+q)-m². After the q=0 subtraction they yield the expressions above. Both tend to q/4 as m tends to zero. For q much smaller than m they instead tend to q²/(6pi m) and q²/(4pi m), respectively. Flavor multiplicity and y² multiply the kernels. Five finite-mass quadratures check the interpolation; these are not a calculation on a nonuniform galaxy background.

For general nu, the massless sheet kernel is nu y²|q|/8. In the hypothetical bulk normalization it becomes beta|q|, beta=pi G nu y²/(2ell). Comparing this to the local cubic term gives

    beta q p / (3alpha p²) = pi q/(4y p).

A derivative expansion therefore requires q << y|p|. The massless kernel applies when the mass cannot regulate this spatial response; it must not be extrapolated into q << m.

As a *dimensional estimate*, in a local deep-MOND point-mass field p approximately v²/r and q of order 1/r, one has m r approximately y(v/c)². At v=200 km/s this is 4.45e-7 y. With y=1, a homogeneous local approximation is consequently inappropriate at that scale. A large y or a different geometric/dispersion construction might alter the hierarchy; neither is selected here. This estimate is not an evaluation of a fractional derivative on 1/r, nor a proof that every gapless completion fails.
